summary.title: You Are What You Read, Even If You Don't Always Remember It
summary.one_liner: Reading shapes your thinking even when you can't recall the books or posts, so the value of reading shouldn't be judged by memory or measurable productivity gains.
takeaways: The goal of a book is to expand your thinking, not to finish it or to remember every detail.
Books and blog posts shape you even when you cannot recall them, much like meals nourish you after you have forgotten them.
Judging reading only by measurable productivity gains undervalues its effect on thinking.
Be mindful of your content diet, since what you read influences you whether or not you remember it.
Education can have lasting value even when specific material is forgotten.
summary.summary: This is a short personal blog post by Jim Nielsen reflecting on why reading matters even when the details fade from memory. He quotes Dave Rupert on expanding your thinking as the real goal of a book, and an Emerson quote comparing books eaten to meals eaten. He extends the metaphor to blog posts and to a content diet. An update adds a reader's anecdote about a professor saying education persists even when nothing is remembered. The page is an opinion essay with no technical content.
